brief.deck: TENEX.AI, the Sarasota-based AI-native security operations firm, closed a $250M Series B led by Crosspoint Capital Partners on 31 March 2026 at a valuation Bloomberg put above $1B, a year after its first customer contract, and named former Charles Schwab CISO Bashar Abouseido President the same day.
brief.the_case_p1: On 31 March 2026 TENEX.AI announced a $250M Series B led by Crosspoint Capital Partners, with Shield Capital and DeepWork Capital, at a valuation Bloomberg reported above $1B. The company stated $25M of contracted revenue within a year of launch and 318% year-on-year growth, first on IT-Harvest's 2026 Cyber 150. The capital funds 250-plus hires in 2026, expansion into Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and deeper Google Cloud SecOps and Microsoft Sentinel integrations. The same day it named former Charles Schwab CISO Bashar Abouseido President. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>A UNICORN BUILDING A GLOBAL BRAND FROM FLORIDA.</font>
brief.the_case_p2: Cybersecurity is the most contested technology lane in Formula 1: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Keeper at Williams, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Red Bull's 1Password, Okta at McLaren, Cato Networks at Alpine and NinjaOne at Audi, with the SentinelOne seat at Aston Martin newly vacated. Managed detection and response is a different product: a round-the-clock security operations service. That leaves Haas, Racing Bulls and Cadillac as open seats, one of them starting from nothing.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The Series B closed on 31 March; a brand budget sized for 250-plus hires and an EMEA launch is being set this quarter. Cadillac settles its second-season partner roster between the summer break and the United States GP in Austin, so an approach in May lands before the 2027 inventory is priced.
brief.why_team_para: Cadillac has no cybersecurity partner and no legacy security stack: its 2026 roster is entirely inaugural, IFS runs the operations software, Core Scientific the data centre and TWG AI the models, and the seat for the service that watches over all of it is open. A debut American team, run from Silverstone while Fishers and Charlotte come online, is standing up its security operation now, exactly when an AI-native SOC is bought. TENEX.AI's Fortune 500 buyers are the audience in the Austin and Las Vegas suites.
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. A race team's attack surface is its data: design files at Silverstone, telemetry from every circuit, supplier links into GM. TENEX.AI would run the team's security operations centre: AI agents triaging every alert, human analysts governing response, cover across US and UK time zones, an incident-response retainer for race weekends, and integration with the Google or Microsoft security tooling the team standardises on. On camera: the pit-wall data it protects.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Cybersecurity Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, covering the move into Fishers and a possible listing window. Estimated $2-4M a year, part in service value. Scope: sidepod or halo placement, naming of the team's security operations centre, Miami, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for CISO customers, a co-authored case study on securing a team from day one.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Foster founded TENEX.AI after three CISO tours and a presidency at Stairwell; he fronts every raise. Path: Bashar Abouseido, President since 31 March 2026; Ryan Shreve, Co-Founder, CFO and COO. No CMO was listed at this date; Richard Rogers joined as CMO on 4 June 2026.
